Title: Philippines' Muslim self-ruled region facing hung parliament
Article:
COTABATO: The Philippines' autonomous Muslim south appeared headed for a hung parliament on Tuesday, unofficial results showed, a day after landmark elections held amid scattered violence.
With nearly every vote counted, none of the parties contesting seats in the 80-member parliament have managed to win the 41-seat majority required to form a government before the Oct 30 opening session.
About 83 per cent of eligible voters turned out for Monday's election, which the country's elections chief hailed as a success, calling residents of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, or BARMM, "fearless."
The two top vote-getters – the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) and the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) – had earned about 35.2 and 32.4 per cent of the vote as of Tuesday evening.
BFP and UBJP officials told AFP they believed they had taken 32 and 29 seats, respectively, under the region's voting formula, which includes both district candidates and party list votes.
The two parties were born of a split within the region's traditional powerbroker, the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), which fought a decades-long war for independence and later self-rule.
The group splintered when President Ferdinand Marcos chose the BFP's Abdulraof Macacua as interim chief minister over the objections of the MILF's senior leadership.
With one precinct having ended its vote at 7pm (1100 GMT) on Tuesday, a coalition of regional political dynasties that garnered the third-most votes – the BARMM Grand Coalition (BGC) – now sits as likely kingmaker.
Moments after he was proclaimed winner of a seat on Tuesday evening, Macacua declined to say if he was already at work attempting to create a coalition.
"We'll cross that bridge when we get to it," he told reporters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court orders family bungalow sold after 15-year sibling dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has ordered the sale of a family bungalow after finding that a bitter dispute among three siblings spanning more than 15 years had irretrievably broken down their relationship.
Judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi said allowing the current arrangement to continue would leave one of the siblings unable to realise his share of the property, resulting in a "continuing injustice".
The court ordered the bungalow, which is held for the equal benefit of Abdul Aziz Al-Akbar Mohamed Noor, 70, and his sisters, Jelinar Mohamed Noor, 65, and Shamsinar Mohamed Noor, 59, to be sold, with the net proceeds divided equally among them.
In her written grounds dated Aug 13, Arziah said the evidence showed that the relationship between Abdul Aziz and Jelinar had broken down irretrievably.
"The parties have been engaged in litigation for over 15 years across multiple forums of civil suits, Syariah court proceedings, and interlocutory applications.
"Jelina herself acknowledged in her affidavit that Abdul Aziz and Shamsinar have severed ties with her," she said.
Arziah said the siblings' relationship had deteriorated to the extent that there was no realistic prospect of them cooperating over the property.
The bungalow was purchased by their late father for the equal benefit of the three siblings.
Although the property was registered in Abdul Aziz's name, he beneficially owns one-third of it and holds the remaining two-thirds on trust for Jelinar and Shamsinar.
Abdul Aziz, the eldest sibling, moved out in 1990 and had not returned to the property since 2007, while Jelinar had been in exclusive occupation for about 25 years without paying rent to either sibling.
The court found that Abdul Aziz had effectively been prevented from deriving any benefit from his one-third interest.
"Without a court-ordered sale, the Plaintiff will remain a 1/3 owner and trustee indefinitely, with no practical means of realising his interest.
"This amounts to a continuing injustice," she said.
Abdul Aziz had sought an order for the sale after attempts to resolve the dispute among the siblings failed.
In June 2024, he offered both sisters the opportunity to buy his one-third share for RM4.356 million, based on a valuation of about RM13.07 million.
Shamsinar also offered her share to Jelinar, but Jelinar did not respond to either offer.
Arziah said Jelinar would not be prejudiced by the sale as she would receive the value of her one-third share from the proceeds.
She also noted that Jelinar was free to purchase the other siblings' interests if she wished to retain the bungalow.
"The advanced ages of all three siblings make it imperative that this matter be resolved within the current generation," she said.
The bungalow is to be sold within 12 months at the best available offer, provided it is not less than 90 per cent of its market value based on a fresh valuation.
Jelinar was also ordered to vacate the property within 60 days.
Abdul Aziz was represented by Ivanpal Grewal while Jelinar and Shamsinar were represented by L. Prakash and Ahmad Shahrizal Abdul Aziz, respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DBKL steps up checks on outdoor dining
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will step up checks on walkways used for outdoor dining to ensure public safety and keep footpaths unobstructed.
Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said DBKL officers and enforcement teams would conduct frequent ground inspections, including at night, to enforce safety clearances and check mandatory compliance stickers.
"To protect pedestrians and wheelchair users, business operators must preserve a clearance of 0.76 to 0.91m on five-foot walkways.
"I want to say that the improvements are made with safety in mind. And therefore, the safety of pedestrians, the safety of the disabled community will not be compromised," he told reporters after a visit to a restaurant in Wangsa Maju.
He said outdoor seating in designated parking bays was strictly banned to eliminate traffic hazards for patrons and restore parking spaces for public use.
Fadlun said enforcement of the updated guidelines would be stricter to ensure customer and pedestrian safety.
Since 2017, DBKL has allowed restaurant operators to set up tables and chairs on five-foot walkways, subject to approval.
[[nid:1533554]]
Last month, DBKL announced new fee structures for restaurant operators, including a RM30 monthly permit per table and chairs.
He added that the public could now lodge complaints against food outlets that occupied walkways or blocked public access.
"Members of the public and resident associations who spot unlicensed outdoor seating, blocked footpaths, or tables placed dangerously in parking bays can submit reports straight to their respective DBKL officers for swift ground action."
Fadlun said complaints had been low in the past, but growing public feedback had prompted DBKL to strengthen its guidelines.
"We are listening to the public as a whole, emphasising that safety will not be compromised.
"Considering the current situation and the incidents reported to us, we feel this strict enforcement is necessary. Any complaint received will be routed directly to the officers to take action on the spot."
Based on DBKL records, 124 permits were approved in 2023, comprising new applications, renewals and appeals.
The number increased to 160 permits in 2024 and 247 permits in 2025.
From Aug 3 to Sept 13, 2026, a total of 27 permits were approved across Kuala Lumpur, generating RM39,123.13 in revenue.

Title: MetMalaysia, Nadma discuss cloud seeding amid haze, falling dam levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) is discussing another cloud-seeding operation with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) amid worsening haze and declining water levels at several dams.
MetMalaysia deputy director-general (Operations) Ambun Dindang said the operation was being considered to increase water levels at dams, while rainfall generated could also help reduce the impact of the haze.
"MetMalaysia is discussing with Nadma to carry out another cloud-seeding operation in the near future.
"This is because we also want to increase the water levels at dams, which have declined, and the possibility of rainfall from the operation could also help, to some extent, reduce the impact of the haze currently affecting the country," he said in an interview with TV3's Buletin Utama.
Ambun said MetMalaysia was monitoring weather conditions and the availability of suitable clouds for the operation.
He also dismissed claims that the haze was caused by volcanic ash from an eruption in Java, Indonesia, saying it was linked to forest fires in a neighbouring country.
"MetMalaysia also confirms that the haze is caused by forest fires in a neighbouring country and not volcanic dust from a volcanic eruption in Java," he said.

Title: 11 Bangladeshis held over fake employment pass syndicate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has busted a syndicate providing electronic Temporary Employment Visit Passes (e-PLKS) and fake police reports at a commercial area in Jalan Chan Sow Lin.
The joint operation, which began at 12.50pm yesterday, involved a team of 40 officers from the Enforcement Division at the Immigration Department headquarters in Putrajaya.
They conducted simultaneous raids on 11 premises at the location.
Its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 11 Bangladeshis believed to be the syndicate masterminds were arrested during the raids.
"They comprised 10 men and a woman, aged between 23 and 48. Initial investigations found that the premises were believed to offer services to prepare suspected fake e-PLKS documents for about RM150 each, while suspected fake police reports were offered for about RM70 each.
"The documents were believed to have been used to deceive embassy officials in applications for Bangladesh international passports," he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said various electronic devices were seized, including 18 laptops, 21 printers and scanners, and three smartphones.
"Also seized were 10 Bangladesh international passports, along with several printed e-PLKS documents and suspected fake police reports," he said.
Meanwhile, follow-up checks around the operation area led to the arrest of 19 more foreigners for various immigration offences.
He said the second group comprised 15 Bangladeshi men and a woman, a Myanmar woman, and two Indonesian women.
"All detainees are currently being held at the Putrajaya Immigration Detention Depot for further investigation. The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passports Act 1966 and Immigration Regulations 1963.
"JIM will not compromise with any party attempting to manipulate or violate the laws of the country," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang Sultan decrees mosques hold special prayers for rain amid worsening haze
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang has decreed that the Pahang Mufti and all mosques perform Solat Hajat (special prayers) and Solat Sunat Istisqa' (prayers for rain) to seek divine relief from the haze.
Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah described the initiative as an effort by Muslims to seek Allah's assistance and mercy, while praying for rainfall to improve air quality.
The Kesultanan Pahang Facebook page said the ruler hoped the people of Pahang, particularly Muslims, would join the prayers for rain to bring blessings, clear the air and end the haze affecting several areas.
"The deteriorating air quality requires due attention and appropriate measures to safeguard the health and well-being of the people," read the post.
As of 1pm today,
all five Air Pollutant Index (API) monitoring stations
in Pahang recorded unhealthy readings, with Indera Mahkota recording the highest at 165, followed by Balok Baru (163), Temerloh (160), Jerantut (159) and Rompin (154).
Kuantan experienced severe haze today, with API readings reaching their highest levels in recent weeks as conditions worsened across the country.
The haze has reportedly been driven by seasonal forest and peatland fires in Indonesia's Borneo and Sumatra.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor may postpone PSRA if haze worsens, says Amirudin
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government may postpone the Primary Religious School Assessment (PSRA) next week if the haze worsens in the state.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the government and Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) would monitor the situation.
"We are looking at the current situation. If it gets worse, we will review. I can't make a direct decision as we need to look at the meteorological report to see the weather and environmental conditions," he said when met after a talk in conjunction with Malaysia Day 2026 at Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Polytechnic.
Selangor has six areas with unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Johan Setia recording the highest at 188, followed by Shah Alam (173), Klang (167), Petaling Jaya (166), Banting (164) and Kuala Selangor (163).
Amirudin, who is also the state education committee chairman, said the state government had parameters to determine follow-up action on the haze, including closing schools if API readings exceed 200.
"If it reaches 200, we will ask schools to close. If it reaches 300, we will also apply for emergency. These are the criteria set, and we will ask schools to close or stop activities.
"Parents will also be advised to take their children home," he said, adding that the state government was arranging for face masks to be distributed for free to students in Selangor.
On a separate issue, he said he was awaiting an audit or review of risky drains in Selangor and confirmed that there was a case of children drowning in Puncak Alam.
He said he had also requested the Kuala Selangor Municipal Council to submit an immediate report and take action to cover the drain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends lower against US dollar as investors await FOMC decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which begins tonight, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the local currency dipped to 4.0835/0880 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0735/0770.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the odds for a US rate hike this week were reportedly at 92.3 per cent based on data from CME FedWatch. CME FedWatch is a tool by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME Group) that shows market expectations for the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest-rate decisions.
"Consequently, the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.25 per cent to 99.641 points while the 10-year US Treasury note yield surpassed the 5.00 per cent level. Other Asian currencies such as the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Singapore dollar were also weaker against the US dollar," he told Bernama today.
At the close, the ringgit weakened against the euro to 4.7111/7163 from Monday's close of 4.7008/7049, fell against yen to 2.6366/6396 from 2.6355/6380, and inched down vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.5037/5098 from 5.4931/4978 previously.
Against its Asean peers, the ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.2093/2131 from 3.2055/2085, and retreated against the Thai baht to 12.2620/2800 from 12.2445/2598.
The local note was also marginally lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 230.7/231.1 from 230.5/230.8 yesterday, and was down vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.48/6.49 previously.

Title: 4 children drowned in Kulim laid to rest in single grave
Article:
KULIM: The bodies of four children who drowned in a drain at Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan, here, were laid to rest in a single grave.
They were buried at the Masjid Jamek Nurul Ehsan Muslim Cemetery at 5.45pm, with around 1,000 family members, relatives and friends attending the funeral.
Earlier, the bodies of Muhammad Aeril Aziz Muhamad Zafis, 12; his half-brother, Muhammad Arif Naufan Abdullah, eight; and Muhammad Iman Nuruddin Khairol Anuar, 10, were brought to the Taman Desa Kayangan Surau at 3.26pm to allow family members and friends to pay their last respects.
The body of another victim, Muhammad Zafril Arsyad Muhamad Azrin, 12, was taken to his family home in Kampung Baru Gajah Merangkak.
The four children reportedly drowned after falling into a drain while attempting to retrieve a ball in an incident at 7.30pm yesterday.
Two of the victims died at the scene, while the other two died while being taken to Kulim Hospital.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP: A-G must explain decision to discontinue case against Muhyiddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General must provide a detailed explanation for his decision to discontinue part of the prosecution against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, said DAP.
DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo said transparency was essential as the case was of significant public interest.
"When criminal charges are brought against any individual, the standard expectation is that the prosecution has thoroughly evaluated the evidence and established a strong basis to proceed.
"The public is entitled to know what specific material factors or legal considerations changed to prompt the decision to halt the process at this stage," he said in a statement.
Gobind said public confidence in the A-G and the integrity of the criminal justice system as a whole would be severely eroded if active, high-profile prosecutions were discontinued midway without clear justification and a full explanation to the public.
Earlier today, Muhyiddin was
acquitted by the High Court
of four of seven charges linked to the Jana Wibawa projects.
He was discharged and acquitted (DAA) of one charge of using his position to obtain RM200 million in bribes and three money laundering charges involving the same amount after the prosecution applied to discontinue the case.
Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin made the ruling after considering the prosecution's application for a discharge without acquittal (DNAA) and the defence's request for a full acquittal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johari represents Malaysia at exchange of Islamic affairs, defence MoUs with Maldives
Article:
MALE: Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani represented the Malaysian government at an exchange of two memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with the Maldives covering cooperation in Islamic affairs and defence.
The agreements were exchanged in the presence of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu at the President's Office here today, following their bilateral talks.
The MoU on cooperation in Islamic affairs was exchanged with Maldivian Islamic Affairs Minister Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed.
A separate MoU on defence cooperation was exchanged with the Maldivian defence minister.
Also present at the ceremony were Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.
The MoU on halal cooperation is expected to strengthen collaboration in the development of the halal industry, including knowledge-sharing, standards, certification, capacity building and promotion of halal products and services.
The partnership could also provide greater opportunities for Malaysian and Maldivian businesses to tap into the growing global halal economy, while facilitating closer cooperation between relevant authorities and industry players in both countries.
The second MoU focuses on maritime security, an area of strategic importance to both Malaysia and Maldives as maritime nations whose economies and national interests are closely linked to the ocean.
Anwar said that as a maritime nation, Maldives places particular importance on maritime cooperation, including security and training.
"Maldives is a maritime nation and places great importance on maritime cooperation, as well as cooperation in security, training and maritime safety, which we will continue to pursue," he told Malaysian media after completing his official programme.
The agreement is expected to provide a framework for closer cooperation between the two countries in strengthening maritime security capabilities, sharing expertise and information, and addressing common maritime challenges.
The two agreements form part of efforts by Malaysia and Maldives to translate their longstanding bilateral relationship into more substantive and practical cooperation.
On Islamic affairs, Anwar said the Maldives' status as an Islamic country provided opportunities to deepen cooperation in areas including halal, dakwah, Muslim affairs, waqf and haj.
At a joint press conference later, Muizzu said the agreements would open new avenues for practical cooperation and further strengthen the institutional foundations of Malaysia-Maldives bilateral relations.
"Today, we witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith.
"These agreements open new avenues for practical cooperation and further strengthen the institutional foundations of our bilateral relationship," he said.
The agreements come as Malaysia and Maldives seek to expand cooperation beyond traditional areas, with both sides identifying new opportunities in trade and investment, renewable energy, digital infrastructure, construction, Islamic finance, tourism, education and the blue economy.
Anwar departed Maldives for Kuala Lumpur at 3.19pm local time today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Viral meal at Bukit Mertajam Hospital was afternoon tea, not main meal
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The viral meal photo involving medical officers on call at Bukit Mertajam Hospital (HBM) showed an afternoon tea serving, not a main meal, the Penang Health Department said.
The department said the serving was one of four meals provided throughout the day — breakfast, lunch, afternoon tea and dinner.
The meals were planned by HBM's Dietetics and Food Services Department, with menus prepared by dietitians and food preparation assistant officers based on the Health Ministry's Hospital Diet, Dietetics and Food Services Manual.
Penang Health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah said the manual provided for four meals a day, with a total daily energy intake of between 1,500 and 1,800 kcal.
"The department and HBM acknowledge and appreciate the public's concern and feedback regarding the provision of food for medical officers on call," he said in a statement.
Dr Zulhizzam said the department understood that the viral photograph could create different perceptions when viewed without the context of the overall food provision.
He said the department and the hospital would continue reviewing areas for improvement to ensure food provision was properly implemented and the welfare of officers on duty remained a priority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: King, Queen urge Malaysians to wear masks amid haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's King and Queen, Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, have advised the public to take precautions and wear face masks amid unhealthy air quality caused by the haze.
In a statement shared on the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's official Facebook account, Their Majesties said unhealthy air quality could affect public health and cause various problems, particularly those involving the respiratory system.
They urged the public, especially senior citizens, children, those with respiratory problems and individuals working outdoors, to take preventive measures to protect themselves from the effects of air pollution.
Their Majesties also advised Malaysians to reduce outdoor activities, particularly when Air Pollutant Index (API) readings reach unhealthy levels.
The public was also advised to drink enough water, remain vigilant of official announcements and monitor daily API readings to safeguard their health and that of their families.
"Their Majesties hope that all Malaysians will continue to prioritise their health and take appropriate measures in dealing with the haze," the statement said.
Smoke from fires in Kalimantan has been carried towards Sarawak by prevailing southwesterly winds, contributing to haze in parts of the state. Haze has also affected several areas in Peninsular Malaysia.
Under the API classification, readings from 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB – Automatic fuel adjustment does not cause sudden hike in electricity bills
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) has clarified that the automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) does not cause a sudden increase in electricity bills, following concerns raised by some consumers on the rising bills.
In a statement, the company explained that the AFA functions as a "two-way mechanism" to adjust for changes in fuel costs and foreign exchange rates.
"When global fuel costs are lower, consumers benefit from a rebate rate, with the savings passed directly to their electricity bills.
"Since the implementation of the new electricity tariff, consumers have received AFA rebates for nine consecutive months, from August 2025 to April 2026," it said.
Conversely when global fuel costs rise, the difference is adjusted through a surcharge. TNB said the surcharge had been imposed since May 2026 due to the crisis in the Middle East.
The national utility company said that the AFA surcharge for September 2026 stood at 3.67 sen per kWh.
TNB said that since the AFA was introduced, consumers have received greater benefits, with a total of RM3.1 billion in AFA rebates compared with RM0.8 billion in AFA surcharges.
"The government has channelled an additional RM435 million through the Electricity Industry Fund (KWIE) to reduce the impact of the AFA surcharge on consumers."
Under the component, consumers with monthly electricity consumption of 600kWh or less are fully exempted from AFA charges, whether in the form of rebates or surcharges.
In addition, consumers within this usage range are also exempted from the eight per cent service tax and retail charges.
Under the new tariff, this group pays about two per cent to 14 per cent less compared with the previous tariff, depending on their level of consumption, added TNB.
"TNB would like to clarify that the AFA does not cause a sudden increase in electricity bills.
"Factors such as festive seasons, school holidays and working from home affect household electricity consumption patterns and, in turn, have a knock-on effect on monthly electricity bills," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China warns against space 'battlefield' after US says weapons deployed
Article:
PARIS: China Tuesday warned against turning outer space into a "battlefield" and Russia said it must be "free from any weapon" after the United States confirmed for the first time that it has arms deployed in orbit above the Earth.
Analysts said that the revelation by Washington confirmed an open secret but the timing of the announcement risked exacerbating tensions with Beijing and the risk of a weapons race in space.
The announcement marked a new stage in the major powers' rush for military space capabilities, driven by rapid technological advancements but lacking a comprehensive legal framework.
"The US has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action," a US Space Force spokesperson said in a statement that did not provide specifics on the weapons.
China's foreign ministry opposed the move, warning against the "weaponisation of outer space, turning it into a battlefield, as well as an arms race there."
"We urge the US side to stop expanding its military capabilities and preparing for war in outer space," ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a news briefing.
Russia called Tuesday for space to be kept "free of any weapons."
"We are counting on broad international consolidation to continue working toward the complete demilitarisation of space," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.
- WHAT ARE THE US CAPABILITIES? -
The US statement did not provide concrete details about what weapons are deployed in space and how many.
"Space control encapsulates the mission areas required to contest and control the space domain – employing kinetic and non-kinetic means to affect adversary capabilities," the statement said.
"These capabilities can be employed for offensive and defensive purposes," it added.
Non-kinetic means could include lasers to blind satellites, or even electromagnetic or cyber jamming of their data links.
- WHY DOES THE US WANT WEAPONS IN SPACE? -
For Washington, both Russia and China – its two main geopolitical rivals – pose potential threats to US interests in space.
China "develops and operates space and counterspace capabilities as part of a military modernisation strategy," according to the US Space Force.
Russia, meanwhile, "views space as a warfighting domain and believes space supremacy will be a decisive factor in future conflicts", it said.
The militarization of space is as old as the space race itself – as soon as the USSR's Sputnik was launched into orbit as the first probe in space in 1957, Washington and Moscow began exploring ways to both arm and destroy satellites.
India in March 2019 said it had destroyed a low-orbiting satellite, following in the footsteps of Russia, China and the US, in a missile test that proved the nation was among the world's most advanced space powers.
- HOW MIGHT CHINA REACT? -
Song Zhongping, an independent military commentator based in Hong Kong and former Chinese army instructor, told AFP the announcement was "no surprise at all" as the fact that the US possesses such weapons "has long been an open secret."
"The only difference is that the US used to keep it ambiguous, whereas now it has gone public, which shows that Washington is no longer trying to hide it," he added.
"China will not stand by and do nothing", he warned, noting Beijing already has its own space station in orbit.
"Whether China deploys weapons in space will depend entirely on whether the United States moves in that direction," he said.
The Wall Street Journal said Beijing supplied Iran with satellite imagery that enabled Teheran to precisely target military facilities and kill US service members in Jordan in July – a claim China has denied.
- CAN WEAPONS IN OUTER SPACE BE REGULATED? -
The biggest worry was once about nuclear weapons in space, but the superpowers and other countries signed the Outer Space Treaty in 1967, banning weapons of mass destruction in orbit.
Since then, Russia, the United States, China and India have explored ways to fight in space outside of that treaty, including by targeting rivals' satellites, which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.
"There is a regulatory vacuum because Article 4 of the 1967 treaty only forbids weapons of mass destruction and nuclear weapons in orbit," said space law expert Laetitia Cesari.
She said the topic would likely be on the agenda at the next UN disarmament meeting in November.
"Moscow and Beijing have been wanting to work for about twenty years on a treaty to prevent the placement of weapons in space," while "Western states are trying instead to work on the notion of responsible behaviour," Cesari said.
The US announcement "will likely give impetus to the restrictive approach that Moscow and Beijing are pushing for," she added.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pestec disputes winding-up petition by SPECO over alleged corporate guarantee
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The board of directors of Pestec International Bhd has disputed a winding-up petition purportedly presented against the company by Shandong Power Equipment Company Limited (SPECO), maintaining that the company has not been validly served with the legal notice.
The company was made aware of the petition after Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd emailed the company a copy of a notice of advertisement published by SPECO in two publications regarding the purported winding-up petition, on Sept 8.
In a filing today, Pestec clarified that it has not accepted or admitted the validity of any purported service of the petition.
"The company reserves all its rights to challenge the Winding Up Petition including the validity of the purported service thereof as well as the underlying claim made by SPECO therein," it stated.
Based on the information available to Pestec, the petition stems from an alleged sum owed by the company under an undated corporate guarantee.
However, Pestec stressed that the claim, including the alleged indebtedness and the enforceability of the purported corporate guarantee, is strongly disputed. The validity of the guarantee is already the subject of an ongoing civil suit commenced by Pestec at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, which was previously announced on Aug 24, 2026.
Pestec further highlighted that it had successfully obtained an injunction against SPECO on Sept 7, 2026. It said that the injunction had effectively restrained SPECO from enforcing any of its rights under the disputed corporate guarantee.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Capital A appoints PCCO managing partner as independent director
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Capital A Bhd has appointed Chuah Sue Yin as independent and non-executive director effective today.
Chuah currently serves as the managing partner at PCCO Group, overseeing its finance and operations.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Capital A said that Chuah holds a registered auditor license approved by the Finance Ministry.
She also holds several other licences including Registered Auditor of Public Interest Entities under Securities Commission Act 1993, Registered Auditor of Co-operative Societies under Section 61 (1) of the Co Operatives Societies Act 1993.
Currently, Chuah is a GRI Certified Sustainability Professional.
Besides Capital A, Chuah holds director positions at BP Plastics Holding Bhd and Tokio Marine Life Insurance Malaysia Bhd.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: What is Jana Wibawa?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Implemented during the Covid-19 pandemic following cabinet approval in November 2020, the Jana Wibawa programme is a continuation of the Bumiputera Construction Contractor Development Programme, which was initiated in 1993.
It is a dedicated development programme for genuine Bumiputera contractors, whereby the members of the board of directors, shareholders and other relevant parties are 100 per cent Bumiputera.
The programme aims to accelerate the implementation of government projects and enhance the capacity of Bumiputera contractors in the construction industry. It is also part of efforts to achieve the objective of strengthening the Bumiputera Economic Community.
To identify companies eligible to participate in the programme, an assessment is conducted in two phases: the first phase at the Ministry of Finance (MOF) level, followed by the second phase at the implementing agency level.
First phase: The committee at the MOF level ensures that all criteria are met by prospective Bumiputera contractors. These include G7 contractors with a CIDB SCORE rating of at least three stars, a good track record, and sufficient technical and financial capabilities. They must also not act as subcontractors to any other party.
Second phase: Eligible contractors who have been shortlisted will be notified to the implementing agencies, such as the Public Works Department, the Ministry of Rural Development, and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage, to invite them to submit bids for projects.
The invited companies will compete to submit the best offers, which will be considered by the relevant Government Procurement Approving Authority. If found eligible, the company will be appointed by the implementing agency.
All processes at the MOF level, particularly those relating to eligibility under the first phase, were carried out in a transparent and open manner.
The first-phase assessment by the MOF was conducted in three stages:
Stage One – Assessment of companies that fulfil the mandatory requirements, namely that they must be Bumiputera-owned, registered with CIDB as G7 contractors in the specified fields, and have a CIDB SCORE rating of at least three stars.
Stage Two – Ensuring that the companies possess sufficient financial capacity, including the minimum liquid capital prescribed according to the value of the project and access to project financing facilities.
Stage Three – Assessing the company's technical capability to undertake the project, taking into account its current work performance and previous work experience, and ensuring that it has no record of troubled projects.
November 2020: The Jana Wibawa programme was introduced under the administration of former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin as a Covid-19 economic stimulus initiative to assist Bumiputera contractors.

Title: Eco World's Singapore unit bidding for Urban Redevelopment Authority land for RM667.6mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eco World Development Group Bhd announced that its unit Eco World Development (S) Pte Ltd had submitted a bid for a parcel of leasehold land at Lorong Punting / Sin Ming Avenue in Singapore.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Eco World said that Eco World Singapore has put in a bid of S$208.1 million (approximately RM667.62 million) for the 4,283 sq metres land to the Urban Redevelopment Authority on Sept 15.
The decision on the award of the tender will be made after all bids have been evaluated, said Eco World.

Title: PAC begins review on implementation of TH RCI recommendations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today began proceedings on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to assess progress in implementing recommendations made in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution.
Its chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the nearly four-hour session involved the senior deputy secretary-general of the Prime Minister's Department, which oversees TH, as well as the institution's chief executive officer and senior management.
She said the session sought updates on the implementation of recommendations in the RCI report on TH's management and operations from 2014 to 2020, which was tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Aug 11.
"This includes issues related to the government's regulatory oversight of TH, as well as its management, governance and financial affairs, particularly in ensuring the institution's long-term operational sustainability amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties," she said in a statement today.
Mas Ermieyati said PAC would recall some of today's witnesses for further clarification and called in the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs), representatives from the finance ministry , agencies under the Prime Minister's Department and Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd.
Mas Ermieyati added that PAC was also finalising several reports, including those on the management of court bail payments through the e-Jamin system and revenue collection from fees and expenditure at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.
Other includes the implementation of the national Research, Development, Commercialisation and Innovation (R&D&C&I) programme and Pelaburan Hartanah Berhad.
"PAC will continue to carry out its check-and-balance role in line with its core function to ensure accountability, particularly for TH and the government as a whole, while restoring the confidence of millions of depositors in TH as a leading institution managing the haj savings" she said.

Title: Tour bus catches fire on North-South Expressway, 15 escape unhurt
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Fifteen people, including a tour bus driver, escaped unhurt after the vehicle carrying 14 passengers caught fire along the North-South Expressway near Yong Peng.
The driver and tour leader managed to evacuate all passengers before firefighters arrived. No injuries were reported.
The incident occurred at 1.25pm at KM137 of the northbound stretch as the bus was ferrying the passengers from Johor Baru to Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang, Selangor.
Yong Peng Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Muhammad Amier Syah Hamzah said the department received a distress call at 1.37pm and dispatched nine firefighters to the scene.
"Upon arrival, the team found the bus on fire, with about 80 per cent of the vehicle destroyed," he said in a statement.
The blaze was fully extinguished at 2.48pm.

Title: Indonesian man first jailed for littering
Article:
JOHOR BARU: An Indonesian man has become the first person in Malaysia to be jailed for discarding a cigarette butt in a public place.
Johor Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said the 36‑year‑old general worker committed the offence in Stulang last February.
He began serving a one‑month jail sentence on Aug 28 after failing to pay the RM1,000 fine imposed by the court.
"The man will undergo a six‑hour Community Service Order (CSO) upon completing his jail sentence," Zainal Fitri said at a press conference after inspecting the implementation of the 50th Series of CSO here today.
Meanwhile, he said 107 cases resulting in CSOs had been disposed of in court to date, involving 59 locals and 48 foreign nationals.
Zainal Fitri said the cases resulted in total fines of RM71,550, with CSOs ranging from two to 10 hours.
He said 3,358 enforcement operations had been carried out in Johor to date, during which 3,095 Notices of Offence (NPK) were issued.
"To date, 789 investigation papers have also been submitted to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further action," he said.
Zainal Fitri stressed that littering in public places is an offence under Section 77A of the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007 (Act 672).
He said offenders may be fined up to RM2,000 or ordered to undergo community service for up to six months, while failure to comply could result in further action, including a maximum fine of RM10,000.– BERNAMA

Title: NST columnist Datuk Rahim Mydin dies aged 75
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: New Straits Times columnist Datuk Abdul Rahim Mydin died today after a long battle with lung fibrosis.
He was 75.
His passing was confirmed by a family member.
The veteran writer was undergoing treatment at the Institute of Respiratory Medicine (IPR) in Kuala Lumpur when he died around 4pm.
A prolific columnist, his opinion pieces ranged from Malaysian nation-building and journalism to racism, migration, international affairs and climate justice.
He was also formerly general manager of Petronas' Group Communications Department.
In 2024, Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, conferred him the Darjah Dato' Paduka Mahkota Perak (DPMP), which carries the title Datuk.

Title: Prosecution closes Muhyiddin's Jana Wibawa case after calling 29 witnesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The prosecution today closed its case against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin after calling 29 witnesses to testify at the High Court here on charges of using his position to obtain bribes.
Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin informed Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin after the final witness, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigating officer Mazery Mohd Zaini, completed his testimony today.
Wan Shaharuddin also informed the court that six prosecution witnesses would be made available should the Bersatu president be called to enter his defence.
"The prosecution has closed its case as there are no more witnesses to be called to testify, and six prosecution witnesses have been offered to the defence.
"The six witnesses are Datuk Dr Marzuki Mohamad, Adam Radlan Muhammad Adam Muhammad, Asmar Asmadi Abdullah Sani, Datuk Seri Asri Hamidon, Datuk Mohd Ayob Mohd Ali and Mohd Shahmeizy Sulong," he said.
The trial, which began on March 9 this year, heard testimony from, among others, former finance minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz and Muhyiddin's former private secretary, Marzuki.
The court fixed Nov 25 for the prosecution and defence to file their written submissions, while the prosecution's oral submissions will be heard on Nov 26 and the defence's oral submissions from Dec 1 to 3.
The proceedings were attended by lawyers Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, Rosli Dahlan and Chetan Jethwani, who represent Muhyiddin.
Muhyiddin, 79, faces three charges of using his position to obtain RM25.3 million in bribes for the party from three companies — Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Mamfor Sdn Bhd and KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd — as well as Azman Yusoff in connection with the Jana Wibawa project.
He is alleged to have committed the offences at the Prime Minister's Office, Perdana Putra Building in Putrajaya, between March 1, 2020 and Aug 20, 2021, under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, which carries a maximum 20-year jail term and a fine of five times the value of the bribe or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
Earlier, the court discharged and acquitted Muhyiddin of one charge of using his position to obtain RM200 million in bribes and three money laundering charges involving the same amount after the prosecution informed the court that it would not proceed with the case against him in relation to Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd.

Title: Johor SWCorp probes alleged Singapore waste dumping
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor SWCorp is preparing four investigation papers into the alleged
dumping of construction waste
from Singapore at several locations in Pontian last month.
Its director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said no new dumping sites had been identified in Johor, while investigations involving four landowners were expected to take about three months before the papers were referred to the deputy public prosecutor for further action.
"Statements have been recorded from two landowners, while we will obtain statements from the other two to complete the investigation papers," he said after inspecting the implementation of the 50th series of
the community service order involving 26 offenders
at De Stulang here today.
Last month, construction debris believed to have originated from Singapore was found dumped at several locations in Pontian, including Kampung Sungai Karang.
The discovery prompted investigations by SWCorp and other agencies into the source of the waste and those responsible.

Title: Young Malaysians seek better jobs, affordable homes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For young Malaysians, Malaysia Day is not just about celebrating the country they call home, but whether they can afford a home, secure a decent job and build a future here.
As they look towards adulthood, they want a Malaysia that offers better opportunities, financial security and a fair chance to build a future without putting their ambitions on hold.
For Universiti Teknologi Mara student Nik Nur Iman Wahyu Nik Azwadi, 24, the rising cost of living is the biggest challenge facing her generation.
She said higher prices of goods, rent, transport and daily necessities were placing increasing pressure on young people, particularly those entering the workforce.
"Sometimes, salaries do not match the rise in living costs, forcing many young people to cut back on spending and postpone plans such as buying a home or getting married," she told the New Straits Times.
Iman said she hoped the next five years would bring better employment opportunities and salaries that better matched the qualifications and skills of young Malaysians.
She also wanted more young people to be able to afford homes and become financially independent without relying heavily on their parents.
Her biggest hope was for Malaysia to become a country that offers fairer opportunities to the younger generation.
"If these basic issues can be improved, young people will have greater confidence in building their future in Malaysia," she said.
Meanwhile, Khairul Danish Alif Khairul Azma, 22, an intern at a Malay-language daily, said creating more jobs and improving starting salaries should be among the government's priorities.
He said some graduates were still struggling to find jobs despite holding university degrees, while wages needed to keep pace with the country's economic development.
"We need more job opportunities and better starting salaries for those entering the workforce.
"The government needs to create more jobs because there are graduates with degrees who are still unemployed, while salaries should be increased to match the country's economic development," he said.
Khairul also called for a fairer job market, saying graduates should have equal opportunities to secure employment without having to rely on personal connections.
He said the government should remain attentive to the needs of university students and graduates as they transition into working life.
Khairul also raised concerns about the presence of foreign nationals, saying the government should strengthen monitoring and enforcement where their activities affected public order and the well-being of local communities.
"The government needs to monitor and regulate the presence of foreign nationals who use various reasons to remain here, as some of their activities can affect public spaces and cause discomfort among local residents."
Meanwhile, youth-based non-governmental organisation Mandiri representative Alyaah Hani said tackling corruption and leakages should be a priority if Malaysia is to build a fairer future for its younger generation.
She said corruption was not merely about individuals giving or receiving bribes, but also about public funds and national resources being lost through leakages and abuse of power.
"Young people ultimately bear the consequences when funds meant for education, healthcare, public transport, housing and employment opportunities fail to reach the people fully."
Alyaah also called for a fairer system of wealth distribution, including the introduction of progressive taxation and a move towards free, quality public education.
She said such reforms would have little impact if corruption and leakages continued unchecked.
"Mandiri's biggest hope is for Malaysia to become a fairer and cleaner country that puts the interests of its people first."

Title: PTT subsidiary bags RM83.26m earthworks contract from Sime Darby Property
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PTT's wholly-owned subsidiary, Pembinaan Tetap Teguh Sdn Bhd (PTTSB), has secured a letter of award (LOA) worth RM83.26 million from Sime Darby Property (BBR Business Park) Sdn Bhd.
The contract, accepted on Sept 15, entails the proposed construction and completion of earthworks and ancillary works for Phase 1 of Bandar Bukit Raja Stage 4 in Mukim Kapar, Klang.
Specifically, the project covers Package 6 (i34), Package 7 (Main Linkage Road), and Package 8 (i26 and i28), PTT stated in an exchange filing.
Site possession is scheduled to commence on Sept 29, following a pre-possession date of Sept 15. The overall project is slated for completion by March 28, 2028, with an earlier completion date of Sept 28, 2027, set for Package 6 (Advance Unit for i34).
While the award will not have any material effect on the group's net assets, share capital, or substantial shareholdings for the financial years ending June 30, 2027, to June 30, 2028, it is expected to contribute positively to PTT Group's future earnings over the contract's duration.
The company does not foresee any exceptional risks beyond normal operational hazards associated with the project and will take necessary mitigation steps as they arise.
PTT's board of directors expressed that the execution of the LOA is in the best interests of the group. None of the directors, major shareholders, or persons connected to them have any direct or indirect interest in the contract.

Title: [UPDATED] MB: I have no power to remove Negri ruler
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Negri Sembilan menteri besar has no unilateral power to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
In a statement issued after today's state executive council meeting, Datuk Ismail Lasim said the matter must be determined based on the Negri Sembilan Constitution and the principles of constitutional monarchy, rather than political or personal considerations.
He said he was aware of issues regarding a "proclamation" removing the state ruler.
"The menteri besar does not have unilateral power to terminate or vacate the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar," he said.
Ismail said the position and processes concerning the Yang di-Pertuan Besar were specifically provided for under the state's Constitution.
He said a proclamation did not, by itself, create constitutional authority.
"The questions that need to be determined are what is the source of authority for the proclamation, what are the conditions and procedures prescribed by the Constitution, and whether all those conditions have been complied with.
"In the context of Article 10 of the constitution, the constitutional provision establishes a specific framework concerning action affecting the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, including requirements relating to the process and proclamation."
Ismail said his involvement in any process prescribed by the Constitution did not mean he could determine the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar himself.
"Where the Constitution provides a role or requires an action by the Menteri Besar, that role must be carried out within the limits and in accordance with the requirements of the Constitution," he said.
He said the issue was not about who wielded greater political power.
"In a constitutional monarchy, power must derive from the Constitution and the law.
"Each institution, the Royal Institution, the Undang Yang Empat, the menteri besar and the state government, have their respective positions and functions, as determined by the Constitution."
Ismail said the central issue was the validity and legal effect of the proclamation.
"The issues that need to be determined are the source of constitutional authority for the proclamation; the conditions and procedures prescribed by the Constitutions; and whether all the conditions and procedures have been complied with so that the proclamation has the legal effect being claimed," he said.
He said an issue of such magnitude should be resolved through proper constitutional and legal processes, including judicial determination if a legal dispute arose.
"A matter of such magnitude must be resolved through lawful constitutional and legal processes, including judicial determination should a legal dispute arise," he said.
Ismail also reaffirmed his respect for the institution of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, the Undang Yang Empat and the Constitution.
"What needs to be defended is not the interest of any individual, but the supremacy of the Constitution, legal certainty and the continuity of the institution of constitutional monarchy.
"The Constitution must be the foundation. The constitutional process must be respected. The institution must be preserved."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain warning issued for 10 states, KL until 9pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in 10 states and Kuala Lumpur until 9pm today.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Sik, Kuala Muda, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap and Baling. In Perak, they include Kerian, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Larut Matang and Selama.
The same warning was issued for Kemaman in Terengganu, while in Pahang the affected districts are Cameron Highlands, Rompin, Kuantan and Jerantut.
In Selangor, the areas affected are Hulu Langat, Gombak, Hulu Selangor, Sabak Bernam and Kuala Selangor, as well as the entire Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur.
Other affected areas include Kuala Pilah and Jempol in Negeri Sembilan, and Kota Tinggi, Kulai, Johor Bahru, Kluang, Mersing, Segamat, Tangkak and Muar in Johor.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Miri (Beluru and Marudi), Betong (Betong and Pusa), Bintulu (Tatau), Kapit (Kapit, Song and Belaga), Kuching (Kuching and Bau), Serian, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Sibu (Selangau) and Limbang (Limbang).
In Sabah, the warning applies to Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Tongod and Telupid), Tawau (Lahad Datu and Kalabakan), Interior Division (Beaufort, Pensiangan, Tambunan, Keningau and Membakut), and the West Coast Division (Ranau, Penampang, Kota Kinabalu and Papar).– BERNAMA

Title: MACC officer retracts police report against Muhyiddin’s lawyer; court decides not to cite for contempt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today decided not to begin contempt of court proceedings against Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation officer Mazery Mohd Zaini, as it accepted the officer’s explanations about his MACC colleague’s police report.
Earlier today, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyers had accused Mazery of contempt of court, due to his actions that led to the police report.
Muhyiddin’s lawyers had pointed out that Mazery was still testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s trial, and should not have communicated with anyone including the MACC colleague who lodged the police report.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin this afternoon delivered her decision on whether to start contempt of court proceedings against Mazery.
The judge noted that she had told all prosecution witnesses in this trial to not discuss matters in this trial with anyone, while they remain on the witness stand.
“But just now, his explanation is that he wants to check that there is no information leak from MACC itself. So it can be said that this witness is overly-cautious and I accept his explanation. I think I will not proceed to cite for contempt.
“But Datuk Amer, it’s entirely up to you if you want to take further legal action, I don’t want to comment on that. But for the court, I accept his explanation,” the judge said towards the end of today’s court proceedings, referring to Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad.
Mazery had testified yesterday and was supposed to continue testifying today, while the police report was lodged by his MACC colleague last night.
Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex on September 2, 2026. Picture by Firdaus Latif
What the police report is about and what happened to it
This morning, Amer highlighted the police report, which he described as a form of “intimidation” against Muhyiddin’s lawyers and an “underhanded tactic” to undermine the trial.
The police report had named Amer as having presented to the court an allegedly classified document, namely Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad’s statement to MACC during investigations.
Amer said however that Muhyiddin’s lawyers did not obtain the document from MACC or through illegal or improper methods, stressing that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had obtained it from Adam Radlan’s lawyers.
Amer said he reserved his rights to take legal action against Mazery, while the latter apologised to Muhyiddin’s lawyers and said he did not intend to tarnish their reputation.
Mazery explained that the police report was lodged to protect MACC’s integrity, as he was worried that Adam Radlan’s statement had been leaked from MACC despite being a classified document.
This afternoon, Mazery returned to the High Court after confirming that there had been no information leaks.
Mazery also confirmed that the police report had been given a “No Further Action” (NFA) status, and a fresh police report had been lodged to withdraw last night’s police report.
“As a result of investigations which I carried out at the headquarters, it was found that there are no information leaks from MACC officers, and I am satisfied that no evidence or documents came from MACC officers,” he told the High Court, saying that last night’s police report had been retracted and has been given “NFA” status.
Mazery also expressed hope that Amer could accept his apology.
KUALAL LUMPUR 16/2/2024 Segambut Bersatu Division Deputy Chief Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad was seen here at Kuala Lumpur Court Complex. PICTURE BY SAYUTI ZAINUDIN
What Mazery told Muhyiddin’s lawyer
After Mazery’s update on the withdrawal of the police report, he was cross-examined by Amer.
Mazery said he had yesterday instructed his subordinate to lodge a police report to determine whether Adam Radlan’s statement had been leaked, but confirmed that this subordinate was not present in court yesterday and would not know what happened in court.
Mazery confirmed that he did not make any checks on whether the document had been leaked before the police report was lodged last night, and confirmed that his checks today with another MACC colleague on whether there had been leaks only took between 15 to 20 minutes.
Mazery confimed he did not contact this MACC colleague yesterday, but disagreed he could have done so before the police report was lodged.
While confirming that he had decided to lodge the police report without first carrying out an internal investigation and without clarifying with Muhyiddin’s lawyers, Mazery denied that the police report was a “deliberate plan” by him to prevent Muhyiddin’s lawyers from asking four recalled prosecution witnesses today about Adam Radlan.
Mazery confirmed that only he and his subordinate had received a copy of last night’s police report, and denied leaking it to a news outlet which had this morning published a news report on the police report.
Among other things, Mazery denied that he wanted to suppress facts that are in favour of Muhyiddin in this case, also disagreeing that the police report was lodged and leaked to the media to deter Amer from pursuing issues linked to Adam Radlan.
Later when asked by lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin to clarify why the initial police report was lodged, Mazery stressed it was purely to check if Adam Radlan’s statement had been leaked by MACC officers.
“So when there is none, I was satisfied that there is none, there is no need to continue with that report, that’s why I made an immediate retraction,” he said, adding that he has no malicious intention and that he had cooperated with both the prosecution and Muhyiddin from the start of investigations until now.
Before the judge delivered her decision on whether to cite Mazery for contempt, Wan Shaharuddin also addressed the police report incident in court.
“As the lead prosecutor in this case, I take responsibility for what had happened today. I myself apologise to Datuk Amer on this incident,” Wan Shaharuddin said, before closing the prosecution’s case in the trial after calling in 29 witnesses over more than 30 days of hearing.
When the trial resumes on November 26 and December 1 to 3, the prosecution and Muhyiddin’s lawyers are expected to present their arguments on whether Muhyiddin will have to enter his defence in this case.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is now facing only three charges of power abuse involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd).

Title: Ringgit slides against euro, yen and pound as greenback gains momentum
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which begins tonight, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the local currency dipped to 4.0835/0880 against the greenback from Monday’s close of 4.0735/0770.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the odds for a US rate hike this week were reportedly at 92.3 per cent based on data from CME FedWatch. CME FedWatch is a tool by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME Group) that shows market expectations for the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate decisions.
“Consequently, the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.25 per cent to 99.641 points while the 10-year US Treasury note yield surpassed the 5.00 per cent level. Other Asian currencies such as the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Singapore dollar were also weaker against the US dollar,” he told Bernama today.
At the close, the ringgit weakened against the euro to 4.7111/7163 from Monday’s close of 4.7008/7049, fell against yen to 2.6366/6396 from 2.6355/6380, and inched down vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.5037/5098 from 5.4931/4978 previously.
Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.2093/2131 from 3.2055/2085, and retreated against the Thai baht to 12.2620/2800 from 12.2445/2598.
The local note was also marginally lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 230.7/231.1 from 230.5/230.8 yesterday, and was down vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.48/6.49 previously. — Bernama

Title: SWCorp: Investigation papers on construction waste dumping from Singapore to be ready in three months
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 – The Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) is currently finalising four investigation papers on the dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian.
Johor SWCorp director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said that the investigation papers are expected to be completed in three months time before being referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further action.
“The probe involves four parcels of land in the affected areas and the statements of two landowners have been recorded.
“We will obtain statements from the remaining two to complete the investigation papers,” he told reporters after inspecting the community service order involving 26 offenders at De Stulang here today.
Zainal Fitri was commenting on SWCorp’s investigation progress into the alleged dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian.
He added that monitoring by his SWCorp showed that there were no new cases of illegal dumping of waste from abroad in other areas.
“So far, there are no new cases reported and investigations will continue for the purpose of prosecution on the existing cases,” he said.
Previously, Pontian district officer Mohd Farid Hassan was reported saying that the locations identified as dumping sites for the construction waste included Kampung Sungai Karang, Kampung Sungai Senai, and Kampung Simpang Kiri.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said that a special committee — comprising the local authorities, police, district office and SWCorp — have conducted a comprehensive investigation into the issue.
On the community service order, Zainal Fitri said that the latest session involved 12 locals, while the remaining 14 were non-citizens, comprising seven Bangladeshis, three Nepalis, three Indonesians, and one Pakistani.
He said the cases involved minor littering offences in public areas, comprising 25 instances of discarding cigarette butts and one instance of discarding a beverage can.
“This community service order is part of an enforcement approach via legal channels that not only has a rehabilitative effect on offenders but also aims to educate the public on the importance of maintaining public cleanliness.
“It’s  implementation is not merely a punishment, but a direct civic education approach for offenders to understand the impact of irresponsible littering and to foster awareness on maintaining environmental cleanliness,” he said.

Title: Kelana Jaya line operations back on track after morning signal fault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Rapid KL’s Kelana Jaya Line, which was disrupted by a signalling fault this morning, has returned to normal operations and is running according to schedule.
Rapid KL, in a statement today, said that the disruption, detected at 9.14 am at Ampang Park Station, caused a train to stop with its doors not aligned with the platform screen doors, affecting the smooth movement of passengers.
Following the incident, its operations and technical teams took immediate action to restore the affected system and conducted continuous monitoring to ensure operations returned to normal as soon as possible.
“Following the action taken, operations on the Kelana Jaya Line have returned to normal, and all trains are operating according to schedule,” it said.
The company is now closely monitoring the signalling system involved to ensure the service continues to operate smoothly and at an optimal level.
Rapid KL also apologised for any inconvenience caused to passengers by the incident. — Bernama

Title: Haze: 39 areas hit unhealthy API levels as of 4pm
Article:

According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy air quality, with Johan Setia recording the highest reading at 188, followed by Shah Alam (173), Klang (167), Petaling Jaya (166), Banting (164) and Kuala Selangor (163).
Two areas in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Serian (171) and Samarahan (151).
In Johor, seven areas recorded unhealthy API levels, namely Tangkak (172), Pasir Gudang (167), Kota Tinggi (164), Larkin (161), Batu Pahat (160), Pengerang (160) and Segamat (117).
Pahang recorded five areas with unhealthy air quality, involving Indera Mahkota Kuantan (167), Temerloh (163), Jerantut (163), Balok Baru Kuantan (162) and Rompin (154).
In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy readings - Nilai (176), Seremban (172) and Port Dickson (159).

An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 301 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin relieved after acquittal on four charges, hopes to be freed from three remaining charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin today expressed relief after the High Court decided to acquit him on four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd.
Thanking his lawyers and also expressing gratitude to Allah on his acquittal, Muhyiddin said: “And Alhamdulillah, that decision is a decision that I really welcome, feel relieved as from the start I am of the view that I am innocent.
“So thank you to all who have prayed for my acquittal today,” he told reporters when met at the court complex here.
Muhyiddin expressed hope that he would also be freed of the remaining three charges that he is still facing in this trial.
“Praylah, hopefully the remaining charges that are still outstanding, which today have completed trial, soon there will be submissions in court, and I hope that I am also freed from the other remaining charges,” he said.
Earlier today, the prosecution applied to the High Court to temporarily release Muhyiddin from four of the seven charges in this trial after evaluating the case as a whole, and applied for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on just the four charges.
Muhyiddin’s lawyers had urged for Muhyiddin to be acquitted on those four charges instead.
After considering arguments from both sides, the High Court decided that Muhyiddin should be acquitted instead of merely given a DNAA for those four charges.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin said this was because the prosecution did not give any reasons besides saying it did not wish to proceed with the four charges, and that the prosecution had left it to the court to decide.
“I’m of the view in the interests of justice, the discretion of the court is to be exercised in favour of the accused,” the judge said.
“So with that, the court discharges and acquits the accused from those four charges only. And we will continue with this case, with the three remaining charges related to Jana Wibawa,” the judge had said.
This afternoon, the prosecution closed its case on the three charges after calling in 29 prosecution witnesses over more than 30 days of hearing.
The High Court has scheduled November 26, December 1 to 3 to hear submissions from the prosecution and Muhyiddin’s lawyers on whether the former PM will have to defend himself in this case.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is now facing only three charges of power abuse involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd).
